To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the incidence of acute cardiovascular events during cancer chemotherapy is underestimated and 2) acute myocardial ischemia is the most common cardiovascular complication of cancer chemotherapy.
the use of chemotherapy is associated with a higher risk of acute coronary syndromes and that the use of taxanes is associated with a lower risk of acute coronary syndrome.
the use of chemotherapy in the treatment of cancer is associated with an increased risk of developing acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chemotherapy on the heart.
the role of hypersensitivity reactions in the development of acute coronary syndromes and acute myocardial infarction.

the development of novel therapeutic approaches that will be able to target the molecular pathways involved in the pathogenesis of chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity and, at the same time, will be able to protect cardiac tissue from the toxic insult of chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute coronary syndromes associated with hypersensitivity are rare but real, and their recognition is of paramount importance.
acute coronary syndromes may occur in patients undergoing chemotherapy and that these patients should be closely monitored and treated as appropriate.
hypersensitivity to chemodrugs is a rare cause of acute coronary syndrome and that it should be suspected only when there are no other possible etiologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy is a safe and effective method for the treatment of locally advanced breast cancer.

we have shown that the majority of patients with a hypersensitivity reaction during chemotherapy have a positive IgE response to the drug and that the IgE response can be measured by the skin prick test.

the Kounis hypersensitivity syndrome is the most important mechanism that explains the acute cardiovascular complications of chemotherapy, including those that are associated with the use of monoclonal antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of heart disease is increased by 20 percent for every 10 years a man delays fatherhood.

the majority of the patients who develop cardiotoxicity from anthracycline-based chemotherapy are asymptomatic and the risk factors for the development of cardiotoxicity include age, gender, and pre-existing cardiac disease.
we need more research on how to better identify which patients are most likely to experience cardiac toxicity from cancer therapy.
